history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - keep-or-drop decision needed. Sonagiri ('Golden Hill', also Swarnagiri) is a major Digambara Jain Siddha Kshetra about 15 km from Datia: a hill complex of about 77 white Jain temples (Laghu Sammed Shikhar, spread over ~132 acres) plus about 26 temples in the village below, roughly 103 temples in total (counts vary slightly by source). Temple No. 57, dedicated to Bhagwan Chandraprabhu (the 8th Tirthankara) with an 11-ft idol, is the main shrine; the hill also has a 43-ft Manastambha (Pillar of Pride) and a Jain museum. Tradition holds that King Nangang Kumar and millions of ascetic saints attained moksha here, and saints including Acharya Shubh Chandra and Bhartrihari lived and composed devotional works at the site. name: Sonagiri Jain Temples
town_description: Datia is a historic town in northern Madhya Pradesh, about 25 km from Jhansi, known for the 17th-century Datia Palace (Bir Singh Palace) and as a Shakti-pilgrimage hub with the Pitambara Peeth and the Jain hill complex of Sonagiri nearby.
tradition: Jainism (Digambar) - NOT A HINDU TEMPLE; keep-or-drop decision needed.

travel.airport: Gwalior Airport (~65 km from Sonagiri) is the nearest major airport; Jhansi is an alternative gateway.
travel.railway: Sonagiri Railway Station lies on the Agra-Jhansi rail line; Datia and Dabra are nearby stations.
travel.road: Accessible via the Dabra-Datia Road, on the Gwalior-Jhansi Road corridor; about 15 km from Datia town.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March is the favored period for visiting the hill complex (verify); avoid the hot midday climb.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Opening hours unverified - not found in sources (verify). Shoes must be removed before entering the temple area and climbing the stairs.
